To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the effects of specific competence on labour market outcomes are rather weak, 2) the effects of group functioning on labour market outcomes, especially on employment and on employment in academic jobs, are large and significant, 3) the effects of the Masters’ thesis results are small and not significant, 4) the effects of generic competence on labour market are small, and 5) the effects of human capital acquired during education and work experience on labour market outcomes is rather small.
the effects of generic competence on the labour market are larger than those of specific competence.
the attainment of domain-specific knowledge is important for the quality of the job, but not for employment chances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the value of competence acquired during education.
the value of competence acquired during education, and the value of competence for labour market outcomes.
the effects of specific and generic indicators of competence on the labour market success of young graduates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
generic competence is more important than domain specific knowledge for employment chances.
generic competence is important, but that it is not sufficient to explain differences in employment and job quality.
specific and generic competence are important, but the specific effects of the indicators of competence are dependent on the labour market segment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
generic competence is important for the attainment of jobs, whereas specific competence is important for attaining a good position in the labour market.
the value of specific competence for the labour market seems rather limited and that the value of generic competence seems to be more important.
the value of specific knowledge acquired at the university for labour market success depends on the type of job.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assessment of generic competence during education is an effective tool to predict labour market outcomes.
the value of specific competence acquired in university education is limited for labour market outcomes in the short term.
the assessment of group functioning during the university programme is an important indicator of the ability of graduates to function in a work group.
